Hi Neha,

Thanks for the quick follow-up. We want to hold a single demo for our global trial team — attendees in NZ (Auckland), Sydney, London, and a couple in San Francisco. I know October has DST shifts in APAC this year and someone mentioned the NZ clock change this Sunday may have impacted calendar invites.

Top constraints:
- Our NZ ops team prefers 10:00–12:00 NZDT (local time) to include their morning standup.
- London participants are only possible in the 14:00–17:00 BST window.
- SF engineers (your end) are available 7:00–11:00 PDT.

Can your team propose 2–3 concrete slots that work across those windows, and confirm whether Redwood will have an engineer on the call for a deeper Q&A? Also please send an updated invite — the original one shows the wrong offset for several attendees.

Thanks,
Samira

Head of Trials, Finota Healthcare

Proposed slots (all listed in local times):
1) 2026-10-06 09:30 PDT / 17:30 BST / 03:30 NZDT (next day) — notes: early for NZ, likely outside their morning window
2) 2026-10-06 08:00 PDT / 16:00 BST / 02:00 NZDT (next day) — likely too early for NZ after DST change
3) 2026-10-06 11:00 PDT / 19:00 BST / 05:00 NZDT (next day) — later for NZ but conflicts with their morning

Given the DST shift in NZ (they roll forward this weekend), local times are tricky. Ben, Marissa — can you weigh in on engineering availability and whether we should run two shorter regional sessions instead of one big global demo? I attached a quick timezone_matrix.xlsx and a tentative invite (demo-invite.ics).

Neha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cross-region demo — availability for next week

Thanks — quick availability note from infra: we can field an engineer for a single 60–75 minute demo but only during the US morning window (roughly 07:00–11:30 PDT) that weekday. After 12:00 PDT we have heavy batch windows. If you're set on a single session, the earliest NZ-friendly *real* overlap after their DST cutover would be 2026-10-06 08:30 PDT which is 02:30 NZDT (not within their requested 10:00–12:00).

Two practical options in my view:
- Option A: Two short region-tailored demos (APAC live at 10:00 NZDT — Redwood runs an APAC-focused 45-minute session with an engineer; EU/US get a combined session later the same day).
- Option B: One long session earlier for US/EU and record a focused segment for APAC with live Q&A for NZ at their morning time next day (we can have Marissa facilitate and Ben join for the Q&A).

If we do separate sessions, I can come to the APAC slot at 10:00 NZDT only if we schedule it for our engineer's local night shift (we can rotate). Need to confirm on-call approval.

-Ben
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Hi all — quick note re DST realities: NZ and parts of Australia jumped forward this past weekend (Oct 4), which means calendar clients that don't auto-update will show the old timezone. I still recommend splitting into two shorter, region-tailored sessions to maximize live coverage and avoid the 02:00–05:00 local gap for APAC.

Proposed final plan (clean):
- APAC: 2026-10-07 10:00 NZDT — 45 minutes focused on integration + live data security Q&A. (Redwood team: Marissa + rotating engineer; we will have logs and example config ready.)
- EU/US: 2026-10-06 09:30 PDT / 17:30 BST — 75 minutes full demo (recorded). Engineer Ben joins live.

Samira — if that works we will:
1) Publish two separate invites (one for APAC, one for EU/US) with explicit UTC times attached so calendar apps don't misinterpret offsets.
2) Share a short <10-minute recorded segment of the core flow for APAC in case any stakeholders can't attend.

Also attached is SOW_Draft_v2.pdf for the trial scope; Ben — can you confirm we have capacity for a shorter on-call rotation in APAC for the week of Oct 7?

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
